page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the burstable c8i-flex server family. Built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor platform, it utilizes an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system exposes 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running under a burstable CPU allocation model. System memory is configured with 16 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. A key architectural distinction is its 480 MB L3 cache, complemented by 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches per core. Supported execution extensions include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) and AVX-512 instruction sets.

In benchmark testing, the c8i-flex.2xlarge demonstrates high single-core efficiency. Geekbench text processing achieved top-tier placement with a score of 2979.0, while single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.18 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression hit 14.25 GB/sec, placing in the top 25 percent. The Geekbench single-core benchmark yielded a score of 2157.0, and stress-ng multi-core performance measured 8669.32. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth was measured at 75.84 GB/sec, while write operations reached 49.02 GB/sec. Small language model text generation (135M) executed at 272.78 tokens/sec, though performance reduced to 8.5 tokens/sec on 7B models. Baseline network bandwidth is capped at 2 Gbps with no ephemeral local NVMe storage included.

The burstable CPU model and flex tier offering yield resource density advantages for workloads with fluctuating CPU demand. Primary performance tradeoffs stem from credit-based compute limits under sustained continuous load, limited memory-per-core capacity, and dependence on remote EBS storage volumes. The hardware profile aligns with text parsing pipeline execution, Redis cache clusters, software compilation, static web server deployments, and light inference workloads.
